topic: The Curious Link: Elastic Collisions and the Digits of Pi
target_audience: High school students interested in physics and mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: Elastic Collisions
lecture_lines: Elastic collisions conserve momentum and kinetic energy.
A small block hits a large block.
The large block slides toward a wall.
These laws govern simple mechanical motion.
[Asset: ElasticCollisionDiagram]
animations: Show two blocks using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg], small block (m) and large block (M), on a black background (#000000). Label them with text "m" and "M" in light cyan (#E0FFFF).
Animate the small block (m) moving toward the large block (M) to represent a collision. Add a visual flash effect at the point of impact.
Display the text "Conservation of Momentum: m*v1 + M*v2 = Constant" in white (#FFFFFF) above the blocks.
Display the text "Conservation of Energy: 0.5*m*v1^2 + 0.5*M*v2^2 = Constant" in white (#FFFFFF) below the conservation of momentum text.
Slow down the animation to highlight the exchange of kinetic energy and momentum between the blocks, represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg].

sections.title: The Collisional Setup
lecture_lines: We track collisions between two blocks and a wall.
Mass ratio changes the collision count.
The hamster hits the sumo wrestler.
animations: Create a scene with a wall on the left, a large block (M) represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sumo.svg] in the middle, and a small block (m) represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hamster.svg] between the wall and block M. Label them with "Wall", "M", and "m" in light yellow (#FFFFE0).

Animate the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hamster.svg] bouncing back and forth between the Wall and the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sumo.svg]. Increment a collision counter text "Collisions: 0" in light green (#90EE90) on the screen.

Increase the size of the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sumo.svg] to simulate a significantly larger mass. As the size increases, show the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hamster.svg] bouncing significantly more frequently. Update the counter "Collisions: X" accordingly.

sections.title: The Mathematical Mapping
lecture_lines: Mass ratio 100^n gives n+1 digits of Pi.
System phase space maps to circular motion.
Collisions act as a digits calculator.
Pi emerges from simple physical rules.
[Asset: PiCollisionGraph]
animations: Display the equation "M = 100^n * m" on screen in bright blue (#00BFFF). Explain this is the mass ratio rule using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/blocks.svg].
Display the number "31" in bold yellow (#FFD700) and link it to the first two digits of Pi (π) by showing "π ≈ 3.14159..." in white (#FFFFFF).

Visualize a circle on the screen with a line rotating inside it, showing how the phase space of the system maps to the circumference and geometry of a circle, similar to [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/billiards.svg].

sections.title: Visualizing the Unfolding
lecture_lines: Represent velocities as vectors in 2D.
The wedge angle depends on mass ratio.
Light beams hit edges π/θ times.
The system measures Pi geometrically.
[Asset: WedgeAnimation]
animations: Draw two lines originating from a central point, forming a wedge with an angle θ determined by the mass ratio m/M. Incorporate the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mirror.svg] to represent the reflective boundaries of the wedge. Use bright orange (#FFA500) for the lines.
Animate a small dot (the "light beam") bouncing between the two lines of the wedge. The path of the dot should leave a faint trail in light grey (#D3D3D3).
Show the count of bounces in the wedge alongside the value of π, demonstrating that the number of bounces relates to the ratio π/θ.
Slowly change the angle θ of the wedge to show how the trajectory and number of bounces change as the mass ratio shifts.

Highlight the final number of bounces and the corresponding digits of π with a glowing effect in bright magenta (#FF00FF), visually reflecting the results against the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mirror.svg].

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
lecture_lines: Nature hides constants in chaotic systems.
Conservation laws reveal deep mathematical truths.
Physics effectively calculates fundamental numbers.
animations: Display a summary text: "Conservation laws can calculate digits of π." in white (#FFFFFF).

Show the simulation with [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sumo.svg] representing the massive block M and [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hamster.svg] representing the tiny block m, highlighting the massive number of bounces (representing many digits of π).
Conclude with the text "Mathematics hidden in chaos" fading in at the center of the screen in bold, light blue (#ADD8E6).
